title: A study testing SOT109 for the first time in patients, to assess how safe SOT109 is, how well it works, and how the body handles it in patients with advanced colorectal cancer that can not be removed by surgery or is metastatic
official: A first-in-human phase 1/2 trial to evaluate the safety, pharmacokinetics, and preliminary efficacy of SOT109 in patients with advanced unresectable or metastatic colorectal cancer
summary:
Main objective: Part A: SOT109 dose escalation: To determine the maximum tolerated dose (MTD) and recommended phase 2 dose (RP2D) of SOT109. 
Part B: SOT109 dose optimization: To determine the optimal dose of SOT109 for subsequent clinical trials.
Part B: SOT109 dose optimization: To assess the efficacy of two RDOs of SOT109 in monotherapy by objective response rate (ORR).
conditions: Advanced unresectable or metastatic colorectal cancer
criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Adults aged ≥18 years
2. Histologically or cytologically confirmed advanced unresectable or metastatic colorectal cancer
3. Documented disease progression following, or intolerance to, all available standard therapies appropriate for the patient
4. At least one measurable or evaluable lesion according to RECIST v1.1
5. ECOG performance status 0–1. Patients with ECOG performance status 2 may be considered following discussion and agreement with the sponsor medical monitor.
6. Adequate hematologic, hepatic, renal, and cardiac function
7. Life expectancy of at least 3 months
8. Willingness to provide tumor tissue (archival or fresh, if required)
9. Ability to understand and sign informed consent
Exclusion criteria:
1. Prior treatment with SOT109 or known hypersensitivity to study drug components
2. Any condition that, in the investigator’s opinion, would interfere with study participation or interpretation of results
3. Known active or uncontrolled infections (including clinically significant viral infections)
4. Symptomatic or untreated central nervous system metastases
5. Significant cardiovascular disease or clinically relevant uncontrolled comorbidities
6. History of interstitial lung disease or pneumonitis requiring treatment
7. Peripheral neuropathy of Grade ≥2
8. Active gastrointestinal conditions that may affect drug absorption or safety (e.g., inflammatory bowel disease)
9. Major surgery or radiotherapy within a clinically relevant period prior to treatment start
10. Pregnant or breastfeeding individuals
